column1: # Per-model serving profile: what the VENDOR says, not what our house defaults were.
# Researched 4 Sept 2026 from model cards, vendor repos and vLLM recipes, each profile written by one agent
# and then checked against primary sources by a second. Three columns, tab-separated:
#   1. a regex matched against the model directory name
#   3. flags appended to the eval runner (sampling and chat-template controls)
# Why this file exists: the campaign served every model greedily or at T=0.6 with no reasoning parser and
# no template kwargs. Not one of those is right for any model here. Three classes of error it fixes:
#   * the chain-of-thought being scored as the answer (no --reasoning-parser)
#   * sampling far from the vendor's recipe - every card here specifies temperature, top_p and usually
#     top_k/min_p, and top_k/min_p have no slot in the OpenAI schema so they must go through extra_body
#   * thinking silently OFF or ON. Hy3 defaults to no_think; gemma-4 defaults to enable_thinking FALSE;
#     Qwen, Inkling, MiniMax, Nemotron, Ling and Ornith default ON. We were measuring some models in a mode
#     their vendor does not recommend and comparing them with models in the other mode.
# Tag-keyed rows come first, so one checkpoint can be measured two ways. gemma-4's vendor default is
# thinking OFF; turning it on took maths 0.600 -> 0.962 and cost knowledge, long-context and instruction
# following. Both modes get measured rather than assumed.
# Laguna-S-2.1 scored 0.000 with 100% truncation: it emitted 2,048 tokens of unbroken chain-of-thought and
# never closed the block, so the parser handed the scorers an empty answer and every item was marked
# truncated. Two arms now: thinking on with room to finish, and thinking off, which is what a retrieval or
# tool-call item actually needs. The vendor asks that sampling not be hand-set, so neither arm sets it.
